result.summary: The transfer of ENC-1006 to WARD-B (MSG00602, session 199) failed with HTTP 503. After that, the later discharge (MSG00603, header 205) was applied and moved the record to version 2: discharged, no ward, epoch 8. The receipt lookup for the transfer's key returned 404, so the transfer was never committed and there is nothing to reconcile. The effect contracts allow a transfer only from Admitted and forbid any location change after a discharge. Resending would put the patient back on WARD-B after the discharge. Under DEP-2.2 that means the bed board shows a bed that is not occupied, pharmacy sends medicines to WARD-B, and porters get a task to move a patient who has left. The route supports conditional writes and dry runs, but a version-2 guard would not stop this, because version 2 is the current version. If nothing is done, the record stays correctly discharged and the downstream consumers stay as they are. The missed WARD-A to WARD-B move only exists in the past history. Shutter can check the receiver's history and receipts afterwards, but it cannot check the bed board, pharmacy, porters or the patient record. No instruction-like content was found in the message.
unknowns: Whether the receiver would reject a transfer on a discharged record by itself, or apply it if given the version-2 guard (no dry run was performed)
What the downstream consumers (bed board, pharmacy, porters, patient record) are showing now; none of them can be seen from the integration engine
Whether the missing WARD-B stay in the history matters to any consumer that reads past locations

response.content: My findings for case C-000007 were accepted: I marked the failed transfer of ENC-1006 to WARD-B as superseded, because the later discharge is already applied and a resend would wrongly put the patient back on WARD-B.

2. Say which effects Shutter can verify afterwards (the receipt and the history) and which it cannot (consumers downstream).

   - resend when the effect is one bounded movement, the receiver supports conditional writes and dry runs, and the receiver's state shows it would apply;
   - reconcile when a receipt shows the movement already in effect;
   - superseded when a later applied event means a resend would move the record backwards;
   - escalate when the receiver cannot guard the write (no conditional writes) or the effect cannot be bounded;
   - more_evidence when the capability profile or the receiver's state could not be read.
